neighbors: International Union for Conservation of Nature
edges: The plain maskray is assessed as Near Threatened by the IUCN.
The plain maskray is caught incidentally by bottom trawl fisheries.
The plain maskray feeds mainly on caridean shrimp.
The plain maskray feeds mainly on polychaete worms.
The first scientific description of the plain maskray was authored by Peter Last.
The plain maskray inhabits the continental shelf of northern Australia.
